title: Composite exceptional adjunction and tensor-map mate identity
statement:
Fix the finite purity datum [def-pur-conventions]: $p$ prime, $a\geq1$, $q=p^a$, $k_0=\mathbf F_q$, $k=\overline{k_0}$, $\ell\ne p$, a finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with uniformizer $\varpi_E$, $n\geq1$, and $\Lambda=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$. Let $f:X\to Y$ and $g:Y\to Z$ be smooth separated finite-type morphisms of pure relative dimensions $d,e\geq0$ between finite-type $k$-schemes [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism]. Use the small pro-etale derived operations [def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom] and $D^b_{ctf}$ [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. For $h=f,g,gf$, put $\omega_h=Rh^!\Lambda$ and let $\varepsilon_h$ be the standing exceptional-adjunction counit [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image]. Let $\alpha_{g,f}:Rg_!Rf_!\xrightarrow{\sim}R(gf)_!$ be compact-support composition [thm-sf-comp-composition] on bounded-below etale-origin inputs [def-sf-etale-origin-subcategory]. Define $c_{g,f}:R(gf)^!\to Rf^!Rg^!$ to be its specified counit mate [pur9-def-upper-shriek-composition], and $\theta_{h,M}:Lh^*M\otimes^L\omega_h\to Rh^!M$ to be the inverse-projection/counit transpose [def-pur-co-smoothness], with projection map [def-exchange-projection]. Write
$$\sigma=c_{g,f,\Lambda}^{-1}\circ\theta_{f,\omega_g}\circ\mathrm{sym}:\omega_f\otimes^LLf^*\omega_g\longrightarrow\omega_{gf}.$$
Then $gf$ is smooth separated finite type of relative dimension $d+e$, $Rg^!$ preserves $D^b_{ctf}$, and $\omega_g\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$. Every bounded constructible source object used in these adjunctions has an etale-origin witness; its compact-support image is again bounded below of etale origin. The composite adjunction $Rg_!Rf_!\dashv Rf^!Rg^!$ [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction] has counit $\varepsilon_g\circ Rg_!(\varepsilon_f Rg^!)$; $c$ is an isomorphism with transpose $\varepsilon_{gf}\circ\alpha_{g,f}$. The maps $\theta_{h,M}$ on the displayed finite-Tor domains and $\sigma$ are isomorphisms.

Put $T_h=\varepsilon_{h,\Lambda}$ and $W=\omega_f\otimes^LLf^*\omega_g$. The transpose of $c_{g,f,\Lambda}\sigma:W\to Rf^!Rg^!\Lambda$ under that composite adjunction is
$$t: Rg_!Rf_!W\xrightarrow{Rg_!\mathrm{PF}_f^{-1}}Rg_!(Rf_!\omega_f\otimes^L\omega_g)\xrightarrow{Rg_!(T_f\otimes1)}Rg_!\omega_g\xrightarrow{T_g}\Lambda_Z.$$
For $K\in D^b_{ctf}(Z,\Lambda)$ let $r_K$ be the canonical tensor reassociation
$$L(gf)^*K\otimes^LW\xrightarrow{\sim}Lf^*(Lg^*K\otimes^L\omega_g)\otimes^L\omega_f,$$
using the derived pullback compositor [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition]. The following identity holds naturally in $K$:
$$(*)\qquad c_{g,f,K}\theta_{gf,K}(1\otimes\sigma)=\theta_{f,Rg^!K}(Lf^*\theta_{g,K}\otimes1)r_K.$$
More precisely both sides have composite-adjunction transpose equal to the inverse composite projection map $Rg_!Rf_!(L(gf)^*K\otimes^LW)\to Rg_!Rf_!W\otimes^LK$, followed by $t\otimes1_K$ and the coefficient-unit map $\Lambda_Z\otimes^LK\to K$. The composite inverse projection here is the successive inverse projection for $f$ and $g$, including the same tensor symmetries and pullback associators.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sbc-smooth-relative-dimension-permanence](2) to $f,g$: $h=gf$ is smooth of pure relative dimension $d+e$. Separatedness follows from [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence](e), and finite type from [lem-sfb-finite-type-composition-base-change](1). Thus all three morphisms satisfy the hypotheses of the finite-coefficient operations and smooth tensor theorem. None of these assertions requires $X,Y,Z$ to be separated over $k$.

source.place: Steps 1–2, orientation-free tensor comparison and its projection/counit transpose

proof.text: The coefficient unit $\Lambda_T$ is a constant finite free rank-one sheaf in degree zero, hence is bounded constructible with Tor interval $[0,0]$ by [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude]. Apply [cor-pur-general-admissibility-datum](2) to each of $f,g,h$: its hypotheses are exactly separated finite type between finite-type $k$-schemes, so each $Rh^!$ preserves $D^b_{ctf}$. In particular $\omega_f,\omega_g,\omega_h$ and $Rg^!K$ are in their stated finite-Tor categories. The first clause of [thm-pur-cohomological-smoothness], applied separately to $f,g,h$, gives invertibility of the specified $\theta_{a,M}$ for finite-Tor $M$. We do not use that theorem's composition clause to prove the present identity.

source.place: Steps 1–2, orientation-free tensor comparison and its projection/counit transpose

proof.text: By [lem-sf-pullback-tor-amplitude] and [lem-sf-tensor-ctf](ii), $W$, $Lh^*K\otimes^LW$ and $Lf^*(Lg^*K\otimes^L\omega_g)\otimes^L\omega_f$ are bounded constructible of finite Tor amplitude. The same applies to the sources formed with $Rg^!K$ and $Rf^!Rg^!K$. Every bounded constructible source has an etale-origin witness by [lem-sf-proetale-constructible-origin](ii). Its compact-support image is bounded constructible by [prop-finite-compact-support-constructibility], and bounded below of etale origin by [thm-sf-comp-composition]. Consequently all successive Hom bijections in [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image] apply to the displayed objects, including the intermediate $Rf_!$-images; no unrestricted ambient pro-etale adjunction is needed.

source.place: Steps 1–2, orientation-free tensor comparison and its projection/counit transpose

proof.text:
Use the two Hom bijections and [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. Their composite has counit $\epsilon^c_M=\varepsilon_{g,M}\circ Rg_!(\varepsilon_{f,Rg^!M})$. By [pur9-def-upper-shriek-composition], $c_M$ is exactly the transpose of $\varepsilon_{h,M}\circ\alpha_{R h^!M}$, so
$$\epsilon^c_M\circ Rg_!Rf_!(c_M)=\varepsilon_{h,M}\circ\alpha_{Rh^!M}.$$
The isomorphism $\alpha$ identifies the left functors. Apply [det-sp-unique-right-adjoint] on the bounded constructible categories (compact support preserves them by Step 3). It makes this specified, counit-compatible $c$ a natural isomorphism, rather than an arbitrary comparison of the same objects.

source.place: Steps 1–2, orientation-free tensor comparison and its projection/counit transpose

proof.text: Step 2 applies to $M=\omega_g$ and to $M=Rg^!K$ for $f$, as well as to $K$ for $g,h$. Thus every tensor map in the assertion is an isomorphism. Since $c_\Lambda$ and tensor symmetry are isomorphisms, their composite $\sigma=c_\Lambda^{-1}\theta_{f,\omega_g}\mathrm{sym}$ is an isomorphism. This proves the isomorphism assertions without choosing any purity orientation.

source.place: Steps 1–2, orientation-free tensor comparison and its projection/counit transpose

proof.text: Write $q=\theta_{f,\omega_g}\mathrm{sym}:W\to Rf^!\omega_g$. Then $c_\Lambda\sigma=q$. Its transpose through $f$ is exactly $\mathrm{unitor}\circ(T_f\otimes1)\circ\operatorname{PF}_{f,\omega_f,\omega_g}^{-1}$ by [def-pur-co-smoothness]; the two source symmetries cancel. Transposing once more through $g$ composes $Rg_!$ of that map with $\varepsilon_{g,\Lambda}=T_g$, by [def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction]. This is the displayed map $t$, including its unit constraint. In particular $\epsilon^c_\Lambda\,Rg_!Rf_!(q)=t$.

source.place: Steps 1–2, orientation-free tensor comparison and its projection/counit transpose

proof.text:
Put $P_a=Ra_!$, $S_a=La^*$ and $G_a=Ra^!$. Use the canonical symmetric monoidal derived tensors of [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal] and the strong monoidal pullbacks of [lem-pur-derived-pullback-tensor-iso]; their pullback compositor is [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition]. On the bounded constructible source and finite-Tor coefficient domains set
$$\pi^a_{B,M}=\mathrm{sym}\circ\operatorname{PF}_{a,M,B}^{-1}\circ P_a(\mathrm{sym}).$$
These inverses exist by [lem-weil-finite-compact-projection-formula]. To apply its pro-etale clause, take the witnesses from Step 3; [lem-sf-comparison-tor-amplitude](ii) gives exactly the finite Tor hypothesis for their etale representatives. The unit and coefficient associativity equations for these very $\pi$ are [lem-pur-projection-formula-coefficient-coherence]; their naturality follows from the naturality of the specified projection transformations [def-exchange-projection]. Thus these are projection formulas on the full domains needed by the restricted-domain clause of [lem-pur-composite-tensor-transpose].

source.place: Steps 1–2, orientation-free tensor comparison and its projection/counit transpose

proof.text:
The schemes $X,Y,Z$ are Noetherian by [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-over-noetherian], applied over the Noetherian field spectrum, hence quasi-compact and quasi-separated by [lem-weil-pbc-locally-noetherian-quasi-separated]. Choose a compactification of $g$ by [thm-nagata-compactification] and a compatible triangle by [lem-weil-pbc-compatible-compactification-triangle]. Apply [lem-sf-composition-projection-mate] on this triangle. Its finite-level identity applies to our specified pro-etale projection maps, including arbitrary ambient inputs before restricting to Step 3's domains. Inverting its projection components gives
$$(1_K\otimes\alpha_{M})\pi^c_{K,M}=\pi^h_{K,M}\;\alpha_{S_hK\otimes M},\qquad
\pi^c_{K,M}=\pi^g_{K,P_fM}\,P_g(\pi^f_{S_gK,M}),$$
with tensor symmetries and the pullback compositor inserted. This identifies the inverse composite projection with the successive inverses for $f,g$, for the actual compact-support compositor. Its independence of the chosen triangle is part of the cited normalized composition identity.

source.place: Steps 1–2, orientation-free tensor comparison and its projection/counit transpose

proof.text:
Apply the restricted-domain clause of [lem-pur-composite-tensor-transpose] to $S_f,S_g,P_f,P_g,G_f,G_g$ and the projection formulas of Step 7. Step 3 checks every Hom-bijection domain, including each compact-support image; Steps 7–8 supply the tensor and projection coherence equations. Its maps $\tau^f_B,\tau^g_B$ are exactly $\theta_{f,B},\theta_{g,B}$ by [def-pur-co-smoothness]: the coefficient-left convention for $\pi$ simply writes the same counit transpose using symmetry. Set $V=\omega_g$, $U=S_fV\otimes\omega_f$ and $q'=\theta_{f,V}:U\to G_fV$. The lemma gives
$$\theta_{f,G_gK}(S_f\theta_{g,K}\otimes1)=\tau^c_K(1\otimes q')$$
and identifies both inverse transposes as
$$P_gP_fN\xrightarrow{P_g\pi^f_{S_gK\otimes V,\omega_f}}P_g((S_gK\otimes V)\otimes P_f\omega_f)\xrightarrow{P_g(1\otimes T_f)}P_g(S_gK\otimes V)\xrightarrow{\pi^g_{K,V}}K\otimes P_gV\xrightarrow{1\otimes T_g}K,$$
where $N=S_f(S_gK\otimes V)\otimes\omega_f$ and unitors are understood. Here $\tau^c$ is formed from $G_fG_g\Lambda$ and the composite counit, not from an independently chosen dualizing comparison.

source.place: Steps 1–2, orientation-free tensor comparison and its projection/counit transpose

proof.text:
Identify $S_h=S_fS_g$ by the pullback compositor, and put $W_c=G_fG_g\Lambda$. Steps 4 and 8 show directly that
$$c_K\theta_{h,K}(1\otimes c_\Lambda^{-1})=\tau^c_K:S_hK\otimes W_c\longrightarrow G_fG_gK.$$
Indeed transpose the left side through the composite Hom bijection: Step 4 replaces the final $c_K$ by $\varepsilon_{h,K}\alpha$, naturality of $\alpha$ moves $1\otimes c_\Lambda^{-1}$ to its source, and Step 8 replaces the projection by $\pi^c$. Naturality of $\pi^c$ in its source factor then leaves $\varepsilon_{h,\Lambda}\alpha P_gP_f(c_\Lambda^{-1})=\epsilon^c_\Lambda$, which is precisely the defining transpose of $\tau^c$. This is an equality by the injectivity of the Hom bijection. Finally $c_\Lambda\sigma=q'\mathrm{sym}$. Precomposing Step 9 with $r_K$ therefore gives exactly $(*)$, with the displayed order of all three factors.

source.place: Steps 1–2, orientation-free tensor comparison and its projection/counit transpose

proof.text:
To identify the more precise transpose in the statement, use the source order $N\cong S_hK\otimes U$ and define
$$b=(1_V\otimes T_f)\pi^f_{V,\omega_f}:P_fU\longrightarrow V.$$
Coefficient associativity of $\pi^f$ in [lem-pur-projection-formula-coefficient-coherence], at $(S_gK,V,\omega_f)$, rewrites Step 9's first two arrows as $P_g(1_{S_gK}\otimes b)P_g\pi^f_{S_gK,U}$. Naturality of $\pi^g$ in its source factor moves $P_g(b)$ past $\pi^g_{K,-}$, giving
$$(1_K\otimes T_gP_gb)\,\pi^g_{K,P_fU}\,P_g\pi^f_{S_gK,U}=(1_K\otimes T_gP_gb)\pi^c_{K,U}.$$
Through $U\cong W$ the morphism $T_gP_gb$ is $t$ by Step 6. Tensor symmetry and the unit constraints of [lem-sf-ringed-derived-closed-symmetric-monoidal] change coefficient-left order to $P_gP_fW\otimes K$ and $t\otimes1_K$. Step 8 says that this $\pi^c$ is precisely the successive inverse projections specified in the assertion. This proves the claimed common transpose, without any assertion that compact support preserves finite Tor amplitude.

source.place: Steps 1–2, orientation-free tensor comparison and its projection/counit transpose

proof.text: All constituent projections, pullback compositors, tensor constraints and counits are natural. The defining Hom bijections are natural as well, so Steps 9–11 give the identity and the stated common transpose naturally in $K$. For $K=\Lambda$ the unit equation reduces the calculation to Step 6. Identities and relative dimension zero require no change; for empty schemes all source objects and arrows in the calculation are zero. Thus no positive-dimension, nonemptiness or absolute separatedness assumption has entered the proof.
